full_caption: Theodora Prendergast, Appellant, v. Amberline Capital Servicing, LLC, Appellee
fictional_notice: FICTIONAL DOCUMENT. Generated for the LegalCase Responder demo corpus. The parties, court, docket number and holdings below are invented and do not correspond to any real case, court, or person.

sections.heading: Paragraph 1
sections.text: This appeal concerns a claimed easement of access across the northern 12 feet of the parcel at 4380 Tanner's Row, Ashbourne, CW, owned by Amberline Capital Servicing, LLC, in favor of the landlocked rear parcel owned by Theodora Prendergast.

sections.heading: Paragraph 2
sections.text: The servient owner retains the right to make any use of the burdened land that does not unreasonably interfere with the easement. Installation of a gate is permissible provided it is not locked against the dominant owner.

sections.heading: Paragraph 3
sections.text: The scope of an easement is fixed by the use that created it. A prescriptive way established by passenger vehicles and light farm equipment does not expand to accommodate commercial haul traffic of the character now proposed by Theodora Prendergast.

sections.heading: Paragraph 4
sections.text: Because the want of access arose from the later vacation of a public road rather than from the severance itself, no easement by necessity was created. The trial court's contrary conclusion was error.

sections.heading: Paragraph 5
sections.text: The common grantor conveyed the rear parcel in 1997 without any reservation of a right of way. At that time the rear parcel abutted County Route 12, which was subsequently vacated by the Ashbourne County Board, leaving the parcel without lawful access.

sections.heading: Paragraph 6
sections.text: Abandonment requires more than mere non-use. There must be an affirmative act evincing an intent to relinquish the right permanently. The fifteen years of non-use shown here, standing alone, does not extinguish the easement.

sections.heading: Paragraph 7
sections.text: An easement appurtenant runs with the land and passes on conveyance of the dominant estate whether or not it is mentioned in the deed. It is extinguished only by release, merger, abandonment, or prescription running against it.

sections.heading: Paragraph 8
sections.text: An easement by prescription requires use that is open, notorious, continuous, hostile and under a claim of right for the full statutory period of 7 years. Permissive use, however long continued, never ripens into a prescriptive right.

sections.heading: Paragraph 9
sections.text: The evidence showed that Theodora Prendergast and predecessors drove a gravel track across the servient estate from 1997 through 2005, maintained it with periodic grading, and installed a culvert at the drainage swale in 2012.

sections.heading: Paragraph 10
sections.text: An easement by necessity arises where (1) the dominant and servient estates were formerly held in common ownership, (2) that unity was severed, and (3) the necessity for the way existed at the moment of severance. Necessity arising afterward will not support the easement.

sections.heading: Paragraph 11
sections.text: Acts of maintenance visible to the servient owner are strong evidence that the use was under a claim of right rather than by neighborly accommodation. The grading and culvert installation here satisfy that standard.

sections.heading: Paragraph 12
sections.text: The judgment declaring a prescriptive easement is affirmed as to the way as historically used, and modified to exclude the proposed commercial expansion. Costs to Amberline Capital Servicing, LLC.

sections.heading: RIDER 1 — GRANT AND DESCRIPTION OF EASEMENT
sections.text: Grantor grants to Grantee, its successors and assigns, a perpetual non-exclusive easement 12 feet in width for ingress, egress and utilities over and across the northerly portion of the Servient Estate, the centerline of which is the existing gravel drive as it presently exists on the ground. This easement is appurtenant to and runs with the Dominant Estate and may not be conveyed separately from it.

sections.heading: Clause 1 — Successors, Assigns and Runs With the Land
sections.text: The benefits and burdens created by this instrument touch and concern the subject land, are intended by the parties to run with the land in perpetuity, and bind every successor in title with notice, actual, constructive or inquiry. A conveyance of the benefited parcel carries the benefit whether or not this instrument is mentioned in the deed of conveyance.

sections.heading: Clause 2 — Interpretation and Construction Against Drafter
sections.text: Headings are for convenience only and do not affect construction. The singular includes the plural. This instrument is the product of negotiation between the parties, and no rule of construction requiring interpretation against the drafting party shall apply. Restrictions on the use of land shall nonetheless be construed in favor of the free use of the land.
